title: Product vs Brand Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 20
description:
A parent bought the bakery's millet laddoos, thinking they were Laddoo Lab's. Both packs looked alike: plain, with a name in small letters. Zoya realises she has a good product, but not yet a strong brand. In this animated lesson we watch Laddoo Lab, a millet laddoo brand from a Bengaluru home kitchen, build its brand piece by piece.

You will see the American Marketing Association's definition of a brand, where the word comes from, and a live build of Dev's brand board: the name tested against Kevin Lane Keller's six checks (memorable, meaningful, likable, transferable, adaptable, protectable), the laddoo-and-leaf logo that still works at coin size, the navy, jaggery gold and cream colours, the tagline, and one pack design for three flavours. We look at why a brand matters to buyers and sellers, and brand elements at work today in a food delivery app, a bank, an airline and a phone maker. The human side: a brand earns trust, but it is a promise, and one broken promise hurts fast. In India, the Trade Marks Act, 1999 protects a registered mark for ten years, renewable again and again.

This is Episode 20 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
